title: "How Awful Is Thy Chastening Rod!"
description: "How Awful Is Thy Chastening Rod!" in Tonic Solfa to ST. FLAVIAN, doh is F: the solfa with the words, staff notation, 10 verses and a piano.
about: Isaac Watts wrote these words for The Psalms of David Imitated in the Language of the New Testament (1719): Psalm 77, part 2, headed “Comfort derived from ancient providences; or, Israel delivered from Egypt, and brought to Canaan”.
Watts' psalms were printed without tunes and sung to any tune of their metre, Common Metre (8.6.8.6). This page sets the words to ST. FLAVIAN; any other Common Metre tune fits them as well.
underlay: "How aw-ful is thy chas-tening rod!" (May thine own child-ren say) "The great, the wise, the dread-ful God! "How ho-ly is his way!"

lines: "The great, the wise, the dreadful God!
I'll meditate his works of old;
I'll hear his ancient wonders told,
And learn to trust his love.
Long did the house of Joseph lie
Long he delay'd to hear their cry,
The sons of good old Jacob seem'd
Israel, his people, and his sheep,
He bid them venture thro' the deep,
And made the waves their walls.
The waters saw thee, mighty God!
Backward they fled, and frighted stood,
Strange was thy journey thro' the sea,
Thy voice with terror in the sound
All heaven in lightning shone around,
Thine arrows thro' the skies were hurl'd;
Surprise and trembling seiz'd the world,
He gave them water from the rock;
Thro' a dry desert led his flock

source: Isaac Watts, The Psalms of David Imitated (1719)
licence: Public domain: Isaac Watts died in 1748.
credits: Words by Isaac Watts (1674–1748), public domain; set to ST. FLAVIAN by NoteFusion, as words-only hymn books were sung.
